title: Phase 6: authored profiles and orchestration assets
description: Author orchestrator and worker role cards, orchestration instructions, and selected skills against the proven CLI per docs/migration.md Phase 6. No raw provider command appears in authored assets. The Phase 6 orchestrator card, not Rust, defaults unsupervised autonomous runs to the red-green evidence-pair policy.

title: Phase 2: abacus-core and abacus-state
description: Implement abacus-core and abacus-state per docs/migration.md Phase 2: pure domain types and rules, then Scribe with SQLite persistence. Acceptance: core tests pure and deterministic; state tests use only temporary directories; Scribe restart, idempotent retry, lease expiry, stale fencing, Acceptance interruption and reconciliation, and migration failure are covered; no br, bv, Herdr, network, or user-home dependency; hermetic budgets recorded.

title: Cargo workspace scaffold (core and state crates)
description: Create the root Cargo workspace with abacus-core and abacus-state crates in their existing top-level folders; abacus-work, abacus-runtime, and abacus-cli crates are added when their phases open. Default tests must be hermetic: no live providers, no network, no user home. Record initial per-module test-runtime baselines per the change-locality rules in docs/migration.md. Acceptance: cargo test --workspace green and hermetic.
notes: Implementation complete and verified locally: root Cargo workspace (resolver 3, edition 2024) with abacus-core and abacus-state crates, forbid(unsafe_code), per-module hermetic test targets, root .gitignore for /target, and docs/test-baselines.md recording warm baselines (core 0.16s, state 0.12s, workspace 0.13s). cargo test --workspace green. Commit pending: blocked by legacy tree-claim contention; close when the commit lands.
close_reason: Workspace scaffold landed: core and state crates, hermetic per-module test targets, recorded baselines

title: abacus-state: transactional semantics
description: Implement leases with stale fencing, sanitized Envelope snapshot persistence, decisions with application receipts and derived reconciliation, Acceptance interruption recovery, and audit events. Cover Scribe restart, lease expiry, stale fencing, and Acceptance interruption and reconciliation per the Phase 2 acceptance list in docs/migration.md.

title: abacus-state: in-memory fake
description: Provide an in-memory implementation of the core persistence ports for use-case tests in other modules, behaviorally matched to the SQLite implementation through a shared contract-test suite.

title: abacus-core: identifiers, roles, lifecycle states
description: Implement domain identifiers, the two first-class role types (orchestrator, worker), lifecycle states, and transition validation as pure deterministic code with no IO and no provider knowledge, per the abacus-core/README.md contract and CONTEXT.md domain language. Tests enumerate legal and illegal transitions as pure unit tests.
close_reason: Identifiers, authority classes, and lifecycle transition validation landed with exhaustive pure test tables

title: abacus-core: assignment, attempt, and evidence model
description: Implement Assignment and Attempt separation with fenced sequential Attempts, bead-content-hash binding, edit-scope conformance types, verification before and after workspace digests, and evidence records including the red-green evidence-pair policy: assert-fail against the declared base using policy-named overlaid verification files with per-file overlay digests, plus the distinct red-errored and red-stale refusals. Ref CONTEXT.md invariants and binding decision 6 in CODEX-HANDOFF.md.
close_reason: Assignment/attempt separation, lease fencing, content-addressed values, edit-scope conformance, and evidence with full red-green pair evaluation landed with distinct-refusal tests

title: abacus-core: typed Signals
description: Implement immutable subject-bound Directive, Report, and Request types. Exposure and discharge derive from immutable call ordering and responding workflow actions; there is no read or ack state and no client-asserted Directive head. Provide derived unresolved-Signal queries as pure functions over ordered records. Ref ADR Decision 8 and CONTEXT I6 and I19.

title: abacus-core: provider-neutral ports
description: Define the persistence, work, and runtime port traits that abacus-cli consumes and that abacus-state, abacus-work, and abacus-runtime implement. No provider types, no SQLite or subprocess knowledge. These traits are the seam every adapter implements; changes here are C1 or above and require cross-review.

title: abacus-core: profile schema and scope checking
description: Implement the profile schema and scope-expression validation per the accepted design from the scope-syntax design bead. Exclusive-scope conflicts are rejected at config validation. Pure validation logic lives in abacus-core; enforcement fencing lives with Scribe.

title: abacus-state: SQLite schema and migrations
description: Design and implement the schema plus migrations for assignments, attempts, signals, evidence, decisions, application receipts, audit events, leases, and repository identity. WAL mode at the git-common-dir abacus/state.sqlite3 path. Migration-failure behavior is explicit. Tests use only temporary directories and databases.

title: abacus-state: Scribe process lifecycle
description: Implement abacus-scribe start, status, stop (and start --foreground), sole-Ledger-writer enforcement, restart recovery, and idempotent request retry. Scribe is a transactional state service only: no manager, messenger, watcher, scheduler, retry loop, or policy engine behavior.

title: abacus-state: client and server transport
description: Implement the versioned local protocol over the per-repository socket under the XDG_RUNTIME_DIR abacus directory, following the outcome of the Scribe socket sandbox probe. Protocol version is checked explicitly; malformed or unversioned requests are rejected with typed errors.

title: Phase 4: abacus-runtime
description: Implement the provider-neutral runtime facade with the pinned Herdr adapter per docs/migration.md Phase 4 and abacus-runtime/README.md. Includes generation-fenced handles (session namespace plus pane plus terminal generation), doorbell delivery, explicit launch environment and cwd, recovery and uncertainty semantics, fake protocol peer, fixture suite, and one explicit live lane. Decompose once the Phase 2 ports stabilize.

title: Phase 1 completion: provider pin gates
description: Close the remaining Phase 1 pin gates recorded in docs/compatibility/ so provider contracts can be locked. Children cover destructive br sync fixtures, independent bv asset verification, Herdr live-agent gates, the approved sandbox execution path, the Scribe socket probe, and the providers lock file. Ref docs/migration.md Phase 1 and the spike gates in docs/adr/0001-modular-architecture.md.

title: Destructive br sync fixtures
description: In a disposable repository against pinned br v0.1.45, exercise sync conflict markers, malformed JSONL, lock timeout, corrupt SQLite database, and interrupted flush and rebuild. Capture sanitized fixtures usable later by the abacus-work contract suite and record observations under docs/compatibility/ (extend 2026-08-04-br-bv.md or add a dated record). Acceptance: each failure path has a fixture plus the adapter-visible error shape; no live repository or global state is touched. Ref the Remaining pin-gate checks in docs/compatibility/2026-08-04-br-bv.md.
notes: Pinned br v0.1.45 destructive gate completed: conflict markers and malformed JSONL reject before mutation (force cannot bypass); external writer yields DATABASE_ERROR busy; corrupt DB error and silent JSONL auto-recovery characterized; SIGKILL flush/rebuild postconditions and retries captured. Seven sanitized fixtures live under abacus-work/fixtures/br-v0.1.45 and compatibility record updated. Disposable roots removed.

title: Independently pin and verify bv release asset
description: Fetch the chosen beads_viewer release asset from upstream, verify its checksum independently, and record release, asset, and sha256 in docs/compatibility/, replacing the current host-path binary identity at /home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin/bv. Acceptance: the compatibility record names an independently fetched, checksummed bv release whose robot contract matches the version 1.0.0 behavior observed in the spike.
notes: Verified upstream v0.18.0 tag commit 44a8e8dd69cad6d0cb8462d2095ed202d993e040. Independently downloaded bv_linux_amd64.tar.gz and checksums.txt; local archive sha256 b8df409c380cc4db9f07cf0329ee8a4d8e669be812528ef1b3b2e0b1260e9145 matched both the published checksum entry and GitHub asset digest. Extracted binary sha256 146313a0a48a6c8a1ba9c3e8c49d75fe820b1a6ce75d474519eac6b8ff27b00d matched the exercised host binary and reported contract 1.0.0. Evidence recorded in docs/compatibility/2026-08-04-br-bv.md; disposable files removed.

title: Herdr live-agent prompt gates
description: Using pinned Herdr v0.7.5, launch disposable real Claude and Codex sessions inside a collision-resistant abacus-spike-nonce named session with an exact pre and post namespace manifest. Verify: agent prompt atomicity for idle and busy agents with exact ambiguity and timeout behavior; state observation when agents block, exit, are killed, and resume through native session identity; live handoff and whether terminal generation is preserved. Install no global hooks or integrations. Record results in docs/compatibility/. Ref the Remaining pin-gate checks in docs/compatibility/2026-08-04-herdr.md.

title: Approved Herdr sandbox execution path
description: The workspace sandbox denies Herdr socket and PTY access while the same high-level CLI works with approved host access. Settle and document the approved way a sandboxed orchestrator invokes the pinned Herdr facade, without moving runtime control into Scribe and without weakening domain boundaries. Ref the Sandbox access section of docs/compatibility/2026-08-04-herdr.md.

title: Scribe socket sandbox probe
description: Confirm a sandboxed Codex agent under workspace-write, and the Claude sandbox, can connect to a Unix socket at the XDG_RUNTIME_DIR abacus repo-id sock path using a disposable stub server (Scribe does not exist yet). If denied, propose the permitted transport for the abacus-state client and server seam before it is implemented. Ref docs/adr/0001-modular-architecture.md open question 1.
notes: Codex probe recorded in docs/compatibility/2026-08-04-scribe-socket.md. Ordinary sandbox denied Unix listen/connect under /tmp and the documented XDG path; loopback TCP also failed. Host controls passed. Official Codex exact Unix-socket allowlisting is the narrow candidate, but a nested v0.146.0 sandbox test still denied it, so fresh-session validation and the Claude reciprocal probe remain. Do not close or implement a TCP/file fallback.

title: Author providers lock file
description: Create .abacus/providers.lock.toml pinning br v0.1.45, the verified bv release, and Herdr v0.7.5 by release, asset, and sha256 identities from the docs/compatibility/ records. Blocked until the bv asset identity exists and the destructive-fixture and live-gate evidence is recorded.

title: Phase 5: abacus-cli vertical slice and abacus init
description: Implement abacus init onboarding and the single CLI vertical slice doctor, ready, assign, spawn, signal, evidence, submit, accept or reject, close on a disposable repository per docs/migration.md Phase 5, including explicit recovery for worker death, Scribe restart, stale lease, dirty handoff, and provider mismatch. No push, PR, merge, CI, or global hook.

title: Phase 3: abacus-work
description: Implement the provider-neutral work facade with the pinned br adapter and optional bv advisor per docs/migration.md Phase 3 and abacus-work/README.md. Includes the lossless ABACUS-to-abacus ID seam, stable-read advice binding, revision hash binding, diagnostics, fake provider, and fixture contract suite. Decompose into child beads once the Phase 2 ports stabilize.
notes: Phase 3 decomposition must mint an explicit child bead for the ADR-0002 seam behavior assigned to abacus-work: reserved key:value label normalization to the single-valued scope map, scope-label-malformed and scope-label-conflict refusals including the provider 50-char whole-label bound, and inclusion of raw declared-key label strings in the bead-content hash. Recorded per Codex C2 nonblocking bookkeeping note on ABACUS-XB0.

title: Scope-expression syntax design
description: Specify how responsibility scopes and routes are expressed and checked (labels, bead subtrees, explicit routes) together with the profile schema documented for abacus-core. Overlap policy is already decided: exclusive scopes are rejected at config validation with Scribe fencing as backstop (ADR Decision 7). Deliverable: a design section or ADR update cross-reviewed by Codex at C2 discipline. Blocks decision-actor authorization work in abacus-state. Ref docs/adr/0001-modular-architecture.md open question 3.
